text:
Mike: quick sync — we need to pick an internal API shape: tiny edge adapters that validate/auth and route, or a central broker that all requests pass through. Major tradeoffs: latency, quotas, telemetry.
Sarah: what's the latency hit if we add an adapter hop?
Leo: adapters add ~2-6ms p95 in my local tests but reduce tail variance vs a central choke. also easier to keep client ergonomics simple (JSON REST in, gRPC inside) if we accept adapters.
Anita: on telemetry and billing accuracy: central broker makes quota/chargeback exact. adapters require reconciliation and can lead to transient overage unless we do frequent sync.
Jordan: also consider protocol choices: if adapters speak HTTP+JSON to clients, should internals be protobuf/gRPC? Protobuf reduces payload size and makes tracing cleaner, but means we need transcoding at edges.
Mike: ops/console needs per-route rollout controls and a "panic" fallback. With a broker we can flip per-route at one place; with adapters we need config distribution and health checks.
Sarah: could do hybrid: adapters handle auth, routing hints, prefix cache; broker handles billing decisions, long-term quotas, and rollout policy source-of-truth. adapters consult broker but use cached policy if broker slow.
Leo: hybrid seems realistic. What about enforcement modes? soft-limit at adapter (allow+tag) and hard-limit at broker (block on reconciliation) — that avoids user-visible errors during transient network issues.
Anita: telemetry envelope: compact protobuf with fields {trace_id, route_id, latency_ms, model_variant, quota_delta, status}. send async to collector; include sampling for high-volume tenants.
Jordan: for wire format, adapters->broker gRPC with proto for speed. Client-facing can remain REST/JSON for SDKs, with an option for gRPC clients in infra teams.
Mike: security: adapters should do token validation locally. Broker only trusts adapter attestation (mTLS + signed config). Audit events still flow to central.
Sarah: console UX: show "adapter sync lag" per region, rollout percent, expected commit vs reconciled usage. Add quick rollback button.
Leo: implementation plan: 1) small POC adapter that validates JWT, routes, emits proto telemetry; 2) broker endpoint for reconciliation + a minimal console toggle; 3) load test to measure p50/p95.
Anita: timeline: two sprints for POC + docs. I'll draft proto telemetry and reconciliation algorithm.
DeployBot: deploy/notify: created branch "pp/hybrid-adapter-proto-poc" and assigned Mike, Anita, Leo, Jordan.
Mike: thanks. I'll open RFC with these notes and include a checklist for rollout and canary metrics.
Sarah: +1. No blockers from my side. :thumbsup:
